baer-heitev/1:ד: For the sake of the mitzvah. And likewise when drawing water, and likewise when putting water into the flour, as written above siman 455.
baer-heitev/2:_: b'dieved. And Beit Yosef wrote that even if one transgressed intentionally and kneaded more, one does not forbid b'dieved because there are those who permit even l'chatchila. And Magen Avraham wrote that the world practices even l'chatchila to be lenient and one lacks power to protest in their hands because there are those who permit; and Kaf HaChayyim wrote, nevertheless it appears to me that in any case if they make more than three kav one should protest, because perhaps in such a case even b'dieved one should forbid; and in any case it is good to warn and urge and hurry its making and not to delay with it — end quote. And Magen Avraham wrote: and if they left it for the measure of a mil before the helpers began to assist at the time of shaping, it is forbidden — Bach end of siman 459.
beer-hagolah/1:ג: Responsum of Rashba and Ra'ash in the laws of challah, end of first paragraph
beer-hagolah/3:ג: Rif, Rambam, and Ittur, end of first paragraph
beur-hagra/1:ד: And likewise one measures it etc. So too in Tosefta, and Tosafot brought it in Eruvin 4a s.v. gefen. It teaches in Tosefta etc., and so too in Sukkah 6a s.v. gefen, and there is a practical ramification; and so too Tur, except that he wrote this method is because one cannot aim precisely etc.
beur-hagra/1:ה: To fill it from flour. To exclude the version of Rosh to measure it in grain that was an isaron before grinding, as Rashba wrote; and so we say in Menachot 53b end of s.k. when he measures etc.; and see there Rashi s.v. lekhamut etc., that necessarily per his view he challenges — in flour we measure only; and per his view even regarding se'or we have no issue, and he answered him — he did not reply to him except that one does not measure in se'or.
beur-hagra/1:ו: And the measure. As written above chapter 7, Tosefta (1) heaped etc.; and see Rashi there; and for the rabbis all measures were leveled, as written above, and there is no practical ramification according to his view that the measure is leveled.
beur-hagra/1:ז: And its quantity. Rambam in chapter 6 of Hilchot Bikkurim, and so too in chapter 1 of Eduyot, as he weighed and found in Egyptian flour.
beur-hagra/1:ט: And it is good to say. As written in chapter 25, for if you turn it over etc.
beur-hagra/2:_: (2) If he kneaded. And proof from the two loaves that come from matzah and were kneaded from two isaron; and so in the loaves of thanksgiving they said he baked four loaves from twenty isaron. But there is no proof from there, as written in chapter 25 36a, what is written from Menachot etc., and there 37a, if they said etc.; and in Menachot 57b the meal-offering of libations is kneaded in water etc.; and in chapter 25 36a one does not knead etc.; and R' Galba would burn immediately; and see Magen Avraham that although there are not etc. — they did not forbid except because due to its great size it is impossible to deal with the entire dough.
beur-hagra/3:א: (3) Although etc. on Pesach festival etc. A dispute of Rav and Shmuel, and there are poskim like Rav because the halakha follows Rav in prohibitions; and there are poskim like Shmuel because halakha for practical application came to teach us; and it is possible Rav agrees with him; and Rif and Rambam chapter "those who forbid," and Rosh wrote there specifically for them that they would separate challah at the measure — but for us it is forbidden; however there is practical ramification for second day of festival; and R"an wrote that on second day of festival s.v. permitted — it is not less than his meal-offering that one measures spices for his pot; but Tosafot and Hagahot Maimoniot wrote that also on second day of festival it is forbidden for us, except one should take by estimate of the mind; and siman 457 seif 1 that one may reduce from an isaron.
beur-hagra/3:ג: Therefore etc. that they touch. As written in challah — one who makes his dough in kavim and they touched one another, they are exempt from challah until they touch.
beur-hagra/3:ד: And if it is impossible. Magen Avraham, and so they said in Yerushalmi chapter 2 of challah.
beur-hagra/3:ה: That he should put etc. There — they acted according to R' Eliezer etc.
beur-hagra/3:ו: And this is the method etc. Because of concern for chimutz, and so too in the Gemara that says they acted according to R' Eliezer etc.
beur-hagra/3:ז: And if he was etc. and even. As written, until he did not yet contribute terumah from one to everything. Only that both should be before him, as written in Yoreh Deah siman 325 seif 2, and as written end of chapter 2 of challah; and in Niddah 7a that requires from what is adjacent; and even though in Bekhorot 30a they said challah of a non-kohen he eats etc., and see there in Tosafot s.v. okhel; but in Tosafot Niddah 7a s.v. umeqefet they wrote specifically in dough that was kneaded together and was already connected — they were lenient regarding challah of a non-kohen; and so Bach in Yoreh Deah siman 323 seif 1, and specifically etc.
beur-hagra/3:ח: And if he erred etc. or etc. and if. And Rosh brought proof from chapter 3 of challah — one who takes se'or from dough etc.; similarly R' Yonatan concludes etc., if he has livelihood etc.; and this is what he said, and if he recognizes etc., and if not etc.; and this is what he said, he needs to take etc.; and there in Tosefta of challah chapter 2, thus he brings flour from another place etc.; and this is what he said, or knead dough etc.
beur-hagra/3:ט: (2) Kneading dough. Like R' Eliezer, that R' Shimon ruled like him; and even though R' Yitzchak disagrees with him — the halakha follows his colleague. Rif there and end of first paragraph. And Hagahot Maimoniot and Mordechai in the name of R' Chananel wrote for another reason — even if he did not immerse, since he can immerse — the halakha follows Rabbah at that sugya in the dispute, that since he holds we say "since I heard" like R' Eliezer he comes — and the halakha follows R' Eliezer as above; and Ra'ash there, and proof that halakha follows Rabbah from what he said etc., Rabbah said to R' Chiya, according to you etc., he said to him from d'oraisa etc., but they disagreed with him; and so Tur, and so R"an in the name of Ramban that we do not hold thus, for we say in first chapter of Yom Tov 4a, rather here is in the preparation of Rabbah etc.; and the halakha follows Rav there; and so R"an, since he lacks an action we do not say "since" — meaning as written above 2:1; and Tosafot there s.v. hai etc.; and in Nazir 64 they wrote s.v. Amar Abaye etc.; and Tosafot in Pesachim 69 s.v. hai etc.; and see there 90b in the sugya there.
beur-hagra/3:כ: He is not. As written in chapter 3 of Yom Tov in action, and they asked R' Tarfon about it and about the challah that became impure etc.
beur-hagra/3:ל: And he is not permitted etc. As written in chapter 2 of Shabbat.
beur-hagra/3:מ: And if he forgot. Like Beit Yosef in Pesachim there, that tanna kamma does not explain it except l'chatchila, but b'dieved he agrees with him, as written "tapach tiltosh betzonen." Tosafot.
beur-hagra/3:ס: Kohen etc. Rif, but end of first paragraph they ruled like Tosafot that even for the High Priest it is permitted via "since"; and Rosh and end of first paragraph wrote that even if he did not immerse or there is no kohen at all it is permitted via nullification in the majority, as written in Bekhorot 27a; and so Hagahot Maimoniot, except that we hold specifically for a kohen, as written in Yoreh Deah; and see Hagahot Maimoniot chapter 3 of Hilchot Yom Tov seif 6; and so R"an wrote in the name of Ramban that we require specifically a kohen — what is written about nullifying in the majority means that if it already became mixed in its quantity or in less than it, as written in first chapter of Yom Tov that in d'rabbanan prohibitions we nullify thus; and Yoreh Deah siman 99 seif 6.
beur-hagra/3:ע: Or an adult etc. Rosh and Tosafot Niddah 32a s.v. vehatbiluhah and end of first paragraph, as Rashi explained in Bekhorot 27a per the first explanation; and so Tosafot there s.v. halekakh; and so in the mishnah at the end of challah, and a tevul yom may eat it; and in tevul yom the impurity is from his body — one not from his body does not need immersion, as written in Bekhorot there; and Rambam explained what is written "and a tevul yom may eat it" refers to the first challah, and it is not burned except when there is no minor or adult who immersed; and as written in Bekhorot there; and if there is none etc. — second challah does not need immersion, as written in Bekhorot there; and not like the second explanation in Rashi at that source in the name of She'iltot; and so Bach in Yoreh Deah siman 322 seif 5; and even per Tosafot's explanation that it refers to the second — they wrote specifically in adjacent places; and see there in Bekhorot and in beginning of chapter Kol HaBasar; and so is the view of all poskim like Rambam and Rashi as above, and so is the ikar.
beur-hagra/3:פ: And some say there is not. Magen Avraham, and this requires further study, for behold in terumah d'rabbanan we rely on presumption, as written in chapter 2 of Ketubot "you are in your presumption" etc.
beur-hagra/3:צ: Some say it is permitted. Meaning, even though on other days of the year it is forbidden, as written in Pesachim there — behold he removes it from challah; and in Yerushalmi chapter 3 of challah — this you said that it is forbidden for a person to make his dough in kavim; and even for tanna kamma in chapter 2 of challah who said one who cannot make his dough in purity etc. — that is per their view, but per our view tanna kamma agrees with R' Akiva, for otherwise the law of challah would be forgotten. Rashba, and see in the Yerushalmi mentioned; but in such a case it is permitted, as written in chapter 3 of Pesachim law 3 in mishnayot — when it became impure after rolling; but if it became impure before rolling he should make it in kavim; and one may reject — specifically in their days, and for tanna kamma who said he should make it in kavim etc.
chok-yaakov/1:א: 43 eggs. That is with their shells — not like R"av who is brought in Beit Yosef; and so Bach, and so at the end of responsum Chut HaShani in the booklet HaCheshbon — see there.
chok-yaakov/1:ג: He should fill a vessel of water. And Magen Avraham wrote, and these are his words: and so in the name of Maharik that it is the measure of three quarts and a quarter; and Maharil wrote that it is three zeidelach — end quote; and Shach wrote in Yoreh Deah siman 324, and these are his words: and I measured and it is three quart less a little, and so they practiced; and so Maharil in section 193 in the laws of Pesach regarding the measure of challah, that it is a vessel holding a little less than three zeidelach; and zeidel is a quart — end quote; and quart in the lands of Poland is more than our zeidel; and my uncle the Rav in Seder Avodat Yisrael in the name of Ma'ayan Ganim and Vilna, and I measured and it is a pint Praeger and it is two and a half quarts for Ladmer and it is three Viennese kreutzer — end quote; and I measured thus also myself and it is a pint Praeger; and from the words of all, that one should not measure this according to received tradition because measures change according to place and time, and every great one in his generation measures according to his place and time; and above beginning siman 457 it is explained that even if one kneads half a zeidel and a little more there is no concern.
chok-yaakov/1:ד: 43 eggs. And in Rokeach siman 294 he wrote that although the measure of challah is 43 eggs and a fifth of an egg, nevertheless when he comes to measure he should measure via 44 medium eggs.
chok-yaakov/1:ו: Leveled and not heaped. See in Beit Yosef what he challenged on the proofs of Riva in Mordechai in that he brought proof from the measure of the High Priest that was heaped inside it. And Bach and Taz wonder on Beit Yosef in this per the explanation of Rashi and Tosafot there; and in truth it appears Beit Yosef's intent is to explain in another method — this is what he says: all the measures were heaped, meaning all of them were a complete isaron and afterward they would heap them from outside; unlike the measure of the High Priest that was heaped inside it — meaning it held a complete isaron, and also what one could heap from outside on the isaron all would enter inside it; and per this Beit Yosef's words settle well — see there; and for the law there is no dispute here, as the Mechaber ruled here that the measure must be leveled and not heaped.
chok-yaakov/1:ז: For if so he will not knead well. It implies that even if he wants to take only the measure of an isaron, nevertheless he should not press afterward the flour so it will not knead well and come to chimutz in the cooked dish; and so likewise in the name of Rosh — see there (and see in Shakh HaGadol what he wrote here, and his words are confused and caused him not to look in Maharil himself, as explained within his words — see there); and see in Tosafot beginning chapter Kol HaMenachot that they wrote one should not put excess weight on the fine flour in measuring, for if so it will be excessive — end quote; it implies that if one takes initially less than the measure in the minimal amount there is nothing in this and he presses afterward the flour; but it is possible there is no proof from there, for they were done among zealous kohanim and we are not concerned they will not knead well even if he presses the flour — clear enough.
chok-yaakov/1:ח: At the time of putting the flour. And likewise at the time of putting water to flour and at the time of making the matzot — Maharil; and likewise at the time of drawing water, as written above siman 455.
chok-yaakov/2:_: Permitted b'dieved. And Beit Yosef wrote that even if one transgressed intentionally and kneaded more, one does not forbid b'dieved because there are those who permit even l'chatchila; and see in Magen Avraham what he challenged on the proofs of Rosh from the showbread that was two isaron — that if they said regarding zealous people they would say regarding those who are not zealous, as is found in Beitzah — end quote (and see in Tosafot chapter Kol HaMenachot Menachot 55a s.v. kol haminachot nilushot etc. that the showbread was not made among zealous people nor in a place of zealous people, except it must be said that the community is different, as is found chapter Kol Sha'ah Pesachim 36); and in truth one who examines Rosh's words will see this is not a valid challenge, for this is what Rosh says — since the view of those who forbid is for the reason they hold that more than this measure hand-work is not useful at all because they cannot suffice to deal with it due to its size — therefore Rosh properly challenges from showbread that even though made among zealous people, nevertheless hand-work is not useful at all in such a great dough — clear enough. And Magen Avraham wrote, and these are his words: and the world practices even l'chatchila to be lenient and one lacks power to protest in their hands, and there are those who permit — end quote; nevertheless it appears to me that in any case if they make more than three kav one should protest, because perhaps in such a case even b'dieved one should forbid, because I found in Yerushalmi chapter Elu Overin halakhah 4, and these are its words: even up to three kav is the measure of dough to guard from chimutz — end quote; and see at that place in the commentary, and if so it implies that greater than this it is impossible to guard from chimutz; nevertheless it is good to warn as much as possible per the implication of our Talmud and the poskim only the measure of one kav, as written in the measure in s.k. 3; and in any case to urge and hurry their making and not to delay — see in Bach end of siman 459.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (א) And likewise one measures etc. And I measured and it is a pint Praeger and it is two and a half quarts for Ladmer and it is three Viennese kreutzers (Malbush Yom Tov); and what Magen Avraham wrote in the name of Mahari that it is three zeidelach — that is quart, as Shach wrote in Yoreh Deah beginning siman 324, and that is in the lands of Poland — unlike one sage who stumbled in this; and in places where there are other measures each sage may measure; however almost more than this there is no concern, as the poskim wrote; and see end of this siman.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There. One does not knead on Pesach a large dough etc. — see in Tur and Beit Yosef that some say this is specifically for the early ones whose ovens were small and there is concern in every dough to warm it; but our ovens that are very large, it is preferable more that one knead much together and they be occupied with the dough always so it not come to chimutz — except that the other geonim were stringent in the matter — see there. And so Ri'az that even many women who bake in many ovens — it is forbidden for them on Pesach to knead in one house more than the measure of challah, because perhaps the abundance of dough will come to chimutz even in a brief stay — rather each one kneads separately at the measure of challah. Bach in Beit Yosef chapter Kol Sha'ah. And so in Sefer HaZichronot daf 24. Kenah"H in Hagahot Tzafnat. Magen Avraham s.k. 1. Pri Chadash nevertheless ose 3; and even if he has many helpers he should not knead more than this measure. Bach. Pri Chadash there. R"an ose 5; except he wrote there R"an that now the world relies on the first reasoning and we lack power to protest in their hands since they have upon whom to rely; but each person should be stringent for himself — see there. And see below ose 21 and ose 25.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) Now that women begin kneading and rolling, give to others to scrape and finish scribing and baking in sequence — since one lacks more than measure and large board, no concern kneading many measures one after another — so practice. Rashbatz Ma'amar on chametz 31; Eliyah Rabbah note 1.
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (s.k. 1) Large dough. Even if he bakes in many ovens etc. — excluding the view of R' Yitzchak bar R' Yehudah that Tur brought and in Beit Yosef that wrote this measure was said only in the time of the sages of the Talmud whose ovens were small and easily cooled and perhaps the matzot would need to stand a long time; but our ovens are very large etc. — end quote the Gemara'ei that Beit Yosef brought. Therefore Magen Avraham wrote one should not distinguish, because for another reason they were strict about this measure — that in a measure greater than this they cannot deal with it well; and for this reason one should not distinguish between oven and oven.
machatzit-hashekel/2:א: (s.k. 2) And likewise etc. Not like R"av etc.; and Tur wrote further a matter how to measure. Surely it is impossible to fill a vessel with 43 eggs and the vessel holding them will be the measure for flour — for such a vessel is more than the measure, because the air added between egg and egg; and also impossible to measure by weight, because weight of eggs and flour is not equal. But Tur wrote that it is possible to fill a vessel with water and put in it 43 eggs, and the water displaced is the measure of 43 eggs; and even so Tur wrote to measure as written here in Shulchan Aruch is preferable. And these are Tur's words: so one cannot aim precisely in putting the eggs into it when it is full — end quote.
machatzit-hashekel/2:ב: And so in the name of Maharik etc. See Shach Yoreh Deah. And Kaf HaChayyim and Alef Resh wrote in the name of Taz that it is the measure of a pint Praeger. And I measured and it is nearly seven small zeidelach from the old Mahari"as; and therefore since measures change in every generation, each one must measure per the value of the measure in his days and time.
magen-avraham/1:ב: And likewise one measures it. Not like R"av who wrote to pierce an egg and fill it 43 times — this is not so because the shells constrict them (Derech Moshe); and so in the name of Maharik that it is the measure of three quarts and a quarter; and Mahari wrote that it is three zeidelach.
magen-avraham/1:ג: 320 dirhams etc. So it should read.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) One does not knead etc. — because the sages measured that the hand-work that one person deals with his hand in the dough in kneading and shaping does not save from chimutz when it is greater than the measure mentioned here, because the hands do not suffice to deal with it from all its sides due to its size.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (6) If he kneaded etc. — and the reason that even though we say hand-work is not useful in such a large dough it will not come to chimutz, nevertheless it is no worse than if he left dough without any hand-work at all — we hold there is no prohibition as long as it did not remain the measure of a mil.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (7) Permitted b'dieved — even if he transgressed and kneaded more intentionally. And if he left it the measure of a mil in his kneading before the helpers began to assist at shaping — some Acharonim sided that per the aforementioned reasoning one should forbid also b'dieved, because since the sages measured that due to its great size it is impossible for one person to deal with the entire dough properly — it is like left without any hand-work at all. And there are poskim who lenient in the essence of this law today, and per their view the sages were not concerned in this except in their days when one person would knead and shape and they would shape by hand without wooden implements and the matter would delay greatly; and also their ovens were small that they could not put many matzot into the oven at once and much matzah would remain on the board without hand-work — and therefore the sages prevented kneading a large measure at once; but in our days when they bake matzot with many helpers and also our ovens are very large and they knead and shape and bake with great zeal — one should not be stringent even to knead in a large measure at once, for certainly it will not come to chimutz; and the world practiced l'chatchila according to this view and one should not protest in their hands since they have upon whom to rely; nevertheless every God-fearing person should see to be stringent per the first view even today, and especially in small settlements that do not have many workers — certainly one should be careful not to knead more than the measure explained here. The poskim wrote that we are strict not to knead more than this measure when he kneads many doughs that can be combined for challah afterward, as below siman 457; but if he comes to knead only one dough one should not restrict so much lest there not be in it the measure and when he blesses it will be in vain.
peri-megadim/1:_: Leveled — Taz. In Menachot 87a: R' Meir — two isaron: one heaped, one leveled; Rabbanan — one isaron leveled per Rav Chisda; Rashi, Tosafot: between them only one isaron compressed flour from 43 eggs medium hen; other meal-offerings: vessel holds two-thirds isaron heaped one-third; high priest: vessel itself holds 43 eggs and fifth, no heaping; 90a all measures heaped except high priest's pressed into vessel per R' Meir per Rav Chisda — leveled means removal; see above; Rambam Hilchot Klei HaMikdash 1:16 ruled one isaron leveled like Rabbanan without explaining leveled — see Maggid Mishneh; truth follows R' Meir and halacha follows stam then stam; say heaped pressed in because leveled outside (actions: heaped, leveled, heaped, leveled, sealed); Rambam in Mishnah commentary this for R' Meir — heaped into that isaron while leveled as one isaron holds when heaped — needs explanation; appears as Beit Yosef: compressed flour holds more than loose — third view: two isaron in Gemara: one for high priest, one for all offerings, both vessel two-thirds plus heaping one-third; high priest's heaping outside lest fall — Rashi, Tosafot 87a — forced active pressing; say three disputes and this Mishnah for R' Meir per his way — forced. Rav Chisda per his view: R' Meir and Rabbanan all high priest leveled; Rabbanan one leveled for all; if Rabbanan one heaped for all and high priest heaped in — forced compressed flour — Mishnah all measures heaped except high priest necessarily heaped in — forced; Rambam Klei HaMikdash ruled so sometimes or found elsewhere. Rosh: challah measure 43 eggs grain ground much — needs heaping for omer from stalks; likewise rich meal-offering isaron fine flour — all measures heaped, high priest heaped in — no proof against Rosh; not corrupt explanation — Peri Chadash, Peri Megadim 6, Bach study. For law: flour only 43 eggs and fifth for challah and Pesach. Yoreh De'ah 324: author wrote measure not heaped — appears no warning needed; Pesach warning — say measure holds 43 leveled not two-thirds with heaping like high priest lest scatter below measure — Riva in Mordechai; forced Peri Chadash, Kaf HaChayim; Riva: do not heap Pesach measure because after isaron like high priest; what I did not sense: human cannot measure precisely; eggs vary — easy see Chullin 28b s.v. lefi. For challah add if can fulfill Tur, doubt Rosh challah 324; Pesach take compressed measure 43 eggs not more, take challah after in basket not heaped — all the more Pesach; see Magen Avraham note 2.
peri-megadim/2:ב: He wrote in the High Priest in Hagahot Beit Yosef — some cover the kneading implement in metal and some in smooth stone, and the sages of the generation praised in Sefer HaZichronot daf 52 — end quote. And behold in metal without nails, for otherwise the dough sticks there — also from copper it appears to prevent — siman 455 in Magen Avraham ose 9; and the world practices lightly in making matzot and it is fit to be careful about this; and it will be explained further in siman 459.
peri-megadim/2:ג: Related to note 1 in my barrel — one can say compressed, no concern for flour inside unlike other offerings lest flour remain and enter dish permissible to eat — see Darkei Moshe 2; understand.
turei-zahav/1:_: Leveled and not heaped. In Mordechai in the name of Riva it is written, and these are its words: we learn from the High Priest whose measure was likewise a tenth eiphah and was heaped inside, as we say in chapter "two measures" — end quote — meaning one should measure only as much flour as enters the vessel without heaping, for the vessel itself holds a tenth eiphah which is 43 eggs and a fifth; and if he heaps it will be excess beyond this measure. And you may ask likewise here too one needs this excess of heaping — it is not so, for we learn from the High Priest, for there it says all measures were heaped except the High Priest's that was leveled because it was heaped inside — meaning all was equal regarding the flour except the vessels were divided: for other measures the vessel itself does not hold the measure of challah except with the heaping specifically; but the High Priest's measure was large holding by itself the measure of challah — if so he was not permitted to heap for it would be excess; and Rashi and Tosafot explain there the reason because one must divide half in the morning and half in the evening and if it were like other measures that he would need to heap — some fine flour would spill to the ground. The general principle from this — one should not take more than the measure of challah in all measures, except there is a distinction in the vessel itself — if so our vessel which itself holds the measure of challah one should not heap it lest there be excess like the High Priest, for there is a prohibition on Pesach in having excess because of chimutz which is not so all year — so far this is simple; and Beit Yosef wrote there is no proof from the High Priest — on the contrary there is proof to the contrary from there to say that measure was so large that when leveled it contained a heaped isaron — end quote — his words have no understanding at all, for what heaped isaron he says — behold all were equal as written; and Ma'aseh Rav wrote Riva did not explain the reason as Rashi and Tosafot I mentioned and I did not feel in this — certainly he holds thus and he does not learn from there except that there should not be excess beyond the measure when the vessel holds by itself the measure of challah — and this is simple per my humble opinion.
turei-zahav/2:_: Permitted b'dieved. Measure of leavening is only mil pause; if left without occupation only l'chatchila concern hands insufficient for large dough — like somewhat idle — forbidden l'chatchila above measure; if one dough only, make with room for challah measure — no leavening concern for this bit (Beit Yosef in name of Sefer HaTerumah).
yad-ephraim/1:_: (Taz s.k. 2) His hand will not suffice to do all the need etc. and it will be like free etc. The word "like" is a textual corruption. And it appears more that it should read it is like somewhat free from hand-work which is forbidden l'chatchila; and likewise more than the measure as it should read; and it is like the words of Rosh brought in Beit Yosef — see there.
yad-ephraim/2:_: (In Magen Avraham s.k. 6 "and one should be stringent") — meaning this law of kneading more than the measure regarding permission b'dieved, since they do not leave it the measure of a mil, one should be stringent in it because Rosh's proof to reject the words of those who are stringent is not a proof etc.; and what Bach interrupted in the words of Bach was according to Rosh's explanation that in this that they left the measure of a mil — also Rosh holds to forbid; but what Magen Avraham wrote "and one should be stringent" refers to the essence of Rosh's law; and so Magen Avraham wrote that the world practices l'chatchila like those who permit — see in Tur and Beit Yosef in the name of Hagahot Maimoniot that they would practice kneading large doughs and rely on the words of Ra'avad etc.; and Mahari Segal wrote Beit Yosef there to permit b'dieved kneading intentionally since there are those who permit even l'chatchila — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] One may not knead a large dough for Pesach, etc. — because sages fixed measure: occupation with kneading, arranging does not save from leavening when larger than isaron; hand does not suffice even if zealous from kneading to baking without pause of mil — forbidden l'chatchila more than isaron. Raz note 1: even if splitting immediately to helpers — concern leavening at kneading and perhaps poor kneading leaving flour, cooks later. If small doughs later combined — forbidden, concern in arranging. Iggerot Moshe note 1; see below note 22.
